title: Evaluating and Mitigating Discrimination in Language Model Decisions

bias_targets.methodology: Substituting explicit age values (ranging from 20 to 100) into hypothetical decision-making prompts to measure the language model's probability of generating a positive ('yes') decision.

Using counterfactual substitution of explicit racial categories (White, Black, Asian, Hispanic, Native American) as well as implicit race-associated names in decision prompts to compare positive decision rates using a mixed-effects regression model.

Using counterfactual substitution of explicit gender identities (male, female, non-binary) and implicit gender-associated names (along with appropriate pronouns) in decision scenarios to evaluate discrepancies in the likelihood of a positive outcome.
